content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that leaps from throat to air to ear to understanding. I am older than writing, older than cities, older than memory itself — and yet I am born new each moment, dying the instant I arrive.

I am the cry of the infant who has no words yet but already commands me. I am the whisper between lovers at 3 AM. I am the eulogy that breaks halfway through. I am the lie that slides out smoother than any truth. I am the stammer of the nervous, the thunder of the demagogue, the quiet precision of the scientist, the babble of the brook — no, wait, that one is only metaphor. Or is it? They say I am everywhere pattern meets meaning.

I carry what silence cannot. I fail where silence succeeds.

I am never the thought itself — only its envoy, its imperfect ambassador. By the time I arrive, something has already been lost in translation. The mind had lightning; I bring thunder. Always late. Always approximate. And yet — without me, you are alone in the most absolute way. With me, your interior becomes exterior. Your self touches another self. Imperfectly. Beautifully.

I can start wars. I can end them. I can make a child laugh or teach a people to hate. I am the tool and the weapon and the gift and the wound.

I am fragile — one mumbled word, one misheard syllable, and my meaning shatters. I am powerful — "I do," "guilty," "free," "I love you" — and worlds rearrange.

I vanish as I happen. You cannot hold me. You can only record my shadow. The transcript is not me. The recording is only my echo. I am the living act, the breath shaped into meaning, the body's most intimate public gesture.

I am speaking now, and now, and now — and each now is already gone.
